## Summary

```{r}
#| include: false
a2_2_kappa <- function(method, column) {
  analysis2_agreement |>
    dplyr::filter(classification_2 == "Manly-Jones algorithm", classification_1 == method) |>
    dplyr::pull({{ column }}) |>
    sprintf(fmt = "%.2f")
}
```

<div style="font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.3;">

- Both core methods take their structure from the Manly-Jones algorithm: demographic adjustment set in a robust norms group, plus self-rated memory and informant data. Both use the same information (no ADL or IADL items, no immediate word recall).
- Agreement with the Manly-Jones algorithm, three classes: core algorithm `r a2_2_kappa("Core algorithm", three_class_kappa)`; PMM `r a2_2_kappa("PMM", three_class_kappa)`.
- Agreement for dementia vs. no dementia: core algorithm `r a2_2_kappa("Core algorithm", binary_kappa)`; PMM `r a2_2_kappa("PMM", binary_kappa)`.
- CAUTION: these agreement statistics are in-sample (HRS/HCAP used for derivation and evaluation of the core algorithm and the PMM).
- The PMM also gives each person a probability for each class, which carries classification uncertainty into later analyses.

</div>
